prompt:
Here are three short samples of my writing. Match my style in what you write.

Sample 1:
making them play lame chicken.... Now all this done by a young lady who remembers eighteen months ago with so much regret that she has lost so much of her high spirits--might argue that her spirits were before tremendous; and yet they were not. That other Sarah was ladylike, I am sure, in her wildest moments, but there is something hurried and boisterous in this one's tricks that reminds me of some one who is making a merit of being jolly under depressing circumstances. No! that is not a nice Sarah now, to my taste.

The commencement of '61 promised much pleasure for the rest of the year, and though Secession was talked about, I do not believe any one anticipated the war that has been desolating our country ever since, with no prospect of terminating for some time to come. True the garrison was taken, but then several pleasant

Sample 2:
for the best for us in the end; that all has come right in spite of us, we will wonder how we could ever have been foolish enough to await each hour in such breathless anxiety. We will ask ourselves if it was really true that nightly, as we lay down to sleep, we did not dare plan for the morning, feeling that we might be homeless and beggars before the dawn. How unreal it will then seem! We will say it was our wild imagination, perhaps. But how bitterly, horribly true it is now!

Four days ago the Yankees left us, to attack Vicksburg, leaving their flag flying in the Garrison without a man to guard it, and with the understanding that the town would be held responsible for it. It was intended for a trap; and it succeeded. For night before last, it was pulled down and torn

of the thing. These men our brothers? Not mine! Let us hope for the honor of their nation that Butler is not counted among the gentlemen of the land. And so, if any man should fancy he cared to kiss me, he could do so under the pretext that I had pulled my dress from under his feet! That will justify them! And if we decline their visits, they can insult us under the plea of a prior affront. Oh! Gibbes! George! Jimmy! never did we need your protection as sorely as now. And not to know even whether you are alive! When Charlie joins the army, we will be defenseless, indeed. Come to my bosom, O my discarded carving-knife, laid aside under the impression that these men were gentlemen. We will be close friends once more. And if you must have a sheath, perhaps I may find one
Write an email to a colleague about a day of worrying news and how you coped. Aim for about 400 words. Reply with the email only.
final_message:
Subject: Yesterday, and what I did with it

Dear Marcus,

You will have heard by now, I am sure, so I shall not rehearse the whole sorry list. But I must tell you how the day went, because I am still not certain whether I behaved sensibly or merely busily.

It began at half past eight with the budget email, which said our team's line was "under review." Now, anyone who has worked here longer than a year knows what that means; and yet I read it four times over, as if the fifth reading might change the verdict. At ten came the news about the vendor, and by noon Priya had confirmed what we had all been whispering in the corridor, that the Hartley contract is not to be renewed. Three blows before luncheon! I confess I ate nothing, and drank a great deal of bad coffee, which is a poor exchange.

The worst of it is not the news itself, but the waiting. We are told nothing, and so we imagine everything. I caught myself drafting my own farewell speech at my desk, and a very touching one it was, too. Then I recollected that I had not been dismissed, and that no one had so much as hinted at it. How absurd we make ourselves!

So here is what I did, in case it is of any use to you. At two o'clock I shut my laptop, a thing I never do, and walked round the reservoir twice. It is a dull walk, and that was precisely its merit. Nothing there asked a decision of me. When I came back I made a plain list of what I actually knew, and what I only feared; the first column was very short, the second ran onto a second page. That told me more than any reassurance could have done.

After that I wrote to the two people on the Hartley account, simply to say that I was thinking of them and that we would sort the handover together. I do not know that it helped them. It certainly helped me, for it gave my worry something to do besides circle.

Last night I cooked a proper dinner, and went to bed before ten. This morning the facts are exactly as they were, but I find I can look at them.

If you are free on Thursday, come to lunch with me, and we will compare lists. I shall bring the coffee, and it shall be good.

Yours ever,
[name]
